t: A Tausug Muslim sultanate ruling the islands between Mindanao and Borneo from Jolo, founded by tradition by Sharif ul-Hashim.
It resisted Spanish conquest for three centuries and grew rich exporting sea produce to China in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries.
Its 1878 grant of North Borneo to a British syndicate is the origin of the Philippine claim to Sabah.
dyk: Paduka Batara, a Sulu ruler who died in China in 1417, is buried at Dezhou in Shandong; members of his family stayed to tend the tomb and their descendants still live there.
ev: Paduka Batara and two other Sulu rulers visit the Ming court; he dies on the journey home
Sharif ul-Hashim founds the sultanate, by Sulu tradition
Spanish forces under Hurtado de Corcuera capture Jolo
Tausug warriors destroy the British post on Balambangan Island
Spanish steam gunboats destroy the Balangingi raiding bases
Sultan Jamalul Alam grants North Borneo to Overbeck and Dent
Jamalul Kiram II gives up temporal power under the Carpenter Agreement

f.predecessor: Tausug chiefdoms of the Sulu archipelago
f.successor: Philippines under United States rule; British North Borneo
